2027-03-16.title: Tuesday of the sixth week of the Great Fast
readings: The servant prays at the well
Christ in you, the hope of glory
2027-03-16.verse: To them God chose to make known how great among the Gentiles are the riches of the glory of this mystery, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
theo: Abraham's servant sets out with ten camels and choice gifts and travels to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor. “He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water; it was toward evening, the time when women go out to draw water.” There, before doing anything else, he prays. It is the first prayer for guidance recorded in the Bible: “O Lord, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today and show steadfast love to my master Abraham.” Then he asks for a sign, and the sign he asks for is wise. He does not ask for the most beautiful girl or the richest family. He asks for a heart: the girl who, when a tired stranger asks for a drink, will say, “Drink, and I will water your camels.” Ten thirsty camels after a desert journey would need a great deal of water drawn by hand. Only a generous, hard-working and kind young woman would offer that. The servant knows that what makes a good wife and mother in Israel is not wealth but a heart like God's own, quick to serve. Before a great decision he kneels his camels, stands by the spring and prays.

Paul shows a different kind of service, the service of suffering: “I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church.” This does not mean that the Cross of Christ was insufficient; his one sacrifice redeemed the whole world. It means that Christ, the Head, wills to share his saving work with his Body. St Augustine taught that the whole Christ is Head and members, and that what Christ suffered in his own flesh is filled up in the sufferings of his members until the end of time (in substance). That is why the Lord said to Saul, “why do you persecute me?” And the heart of it all is “Christ in you, the hope of glory.” In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples a second time: “The Son of Man is to be betrayed into human hands, and they will kill him, and three days after being killed, he will rise again.” Mark adds, sadly: “they did not understand what he was saying and were afraid to ask him.” Holy Week is near. Let us not be afraid to ask him what his Cross means for our lives.
outline: Ask: before a big decision, what do you do first?
The servant asks for a generous heart.
Christ shares his saving work with his Body.
Bringing our questions about the Cross to Jesus.
“Christ in you, the hope of glory.”
live: Before any important conversation or decision this week, stop and pray one sentence: Lord, grant me success today.
Choose one pain or difficulty you are carrying and offer it each day this week for the Church, naming a person who needs grace.
2027-03-16.prayer: Lord God of Abraham, your servant prayed at the well and you heard him before he had finished speaking. Teach us to pray before we choose, and give us generous hearts that serve beyond what is asked. Unite our sufferings with the afflictions of your Son for the sake of his Body, the Church. Let Christ dwell in us, our hope of glory, and do not let us be afraid to ask him the meaning of his Cross. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Head offers himself, and his Body, the Church, offers with him every suffering joined to his: the whole Christ before the Father.

quick: At the well, Abraham's servant prays for guidance and asks for a girl with a generous heart.
Paul rejoices to suffer for the Church, the Body of Christ; Christ in us is the hope of glory.
Jesus foretells his death and rising; the disciples do not understand and are afraid to ask.
2027-03-16.action: Pray one sentence before every important decision today.
2027-03-16.question: What question about the Cross have I been afraid to ask Jesus?

family.explain: Abraham's servant came to a well after a long journey. He did not rush. He made his camels kneel down and he prayed: Lord, help me today. He asked God to show him a kind girl, one who would give water not only to him but to all his camels too. God loves it when we pray before we do important things.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has a big decision to make this week.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do tomorrow that is more than what we are asked?”

illus: In a parish near Pathanamthitta there was an old woman who had been bedridden for eleven years. Beside her pillow she kept a list of names: the parish priest, the seminarians of the diocese, families in trouble. Every morning she said: Lord, today my pain is for these. When a new priest came to the parish, he was taken to see her on his first day. The old priests told him: this room is where the parish gets its strength. He did not believe it at first. After some years he said he did.

pm.open: Lord, we come to the well of your word. Hear us before we finish speaking, and let Christ dwell in us, our hope of glory. Amen.
share: O Lord, please grant me success today (Genesis 24:12). Do I pray before I act, or only after things go wrong?
I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions (Colossians 1:24). What suffering in my life could I offer for the Church?
They were afraid to ask him (Mark 9:32). What am I afraid to ask the Lord?
interc: For all who must make important decisions this week.
For the sick, the bedridden and those in chronic pain, that they may know their suffering is precious in the Body of Christ.
For persecuted Christians, in whom Christ still suffers.
For young people seeking a husband or wife, that they may look for a generous heart.
For all preparing to celebrate Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, your Son foretold his Passion and his Resurrection. Give us courage to ask, wisdom to pray before we choose, and grace to unite our sufferings with his. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham's servant comes to a well after a long journey. Before he does anything else, he makes his camels kneel and he prays: O Lord, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today (Genesis 24:12).

He asks God for a sign: a girl who will say, Drink, and I will water your camels (Genesis 24:14). He is not looking for beauty or wealth. He is looking for a generous heart. That is the kind of heart God looks for in us too.

Paul says something surprising: I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake (Colossians 1:24). Christ's Cross saved the world, but he lets us share in it. When we offer our pain with love, it becomes a gift for the whole Church. And the secret is this: Christ in you, the hope of glory (Colossians 1:27).

Jesus tells his disciples again that he will be killed and will rise. But they did not understand what he was saying and were afraid to ask him (Mark 9:32). Holy Week is coming. Let us not be afraid to ask Jesus what his Cross means for us. He will answer those who ask. Amen.
kids: Children, the servant made his camels kneel down and then he prayed. Before a test, before a game, before you say sorry to someone, you can stop and pray: Jesus, help me today. And try to be like the girl at the well: do a little more than you are asked.

intro: Theme: “Christ in you, the hope of glory.”
The prayer at the well, the sufferings that build up the Body, and the question the disciples were afraid to ask.

sub: The camels kneel; the servant prays.
q: Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths.
If any of you is lacking in wisdom, ask God, who gives to all generously and ungrudgingly, and it will be given you.
points.apply: Pray one sentence before every important choice this week.

q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
points.apply: Offer one daily pain this week for a named person in the Church.

sub: The second foretelling of the Passion.
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Bring Jesus one honest question about suffering or the Cross in prayer before Hosanna Sunday.

concl: The servant prayed before he chose; Paul rejoiced to suffer for the Body.
Jesus foretold his death and rising; he waits for us to ask.
2027-03-16.resolve: Pray before every choice, offer every pain, and ask the Lord the meaning of his Cross.
